editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.
scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 2, verses 11.2.35–11.2.55.

entries.sanskrit: अञ्जः-पदेनोक्तं सुकरत्वं विवृणोति---यान् इति । यान् आस्थाय आश्रित्य योगादिष्व् इव न प्रमाद्येत, विघ्नैर् न विहन्येत । किं च, निमील्य नेत्रे धावन्न् अपि । इह एषु भागवत-धर्मेषु न स्खलेत् । निमीलनं नामाज्ञानम् । यथाहुः--- श्रुति-स्मृती उभे नेत्रे विप्राणां परिकीर्तिते । एकेन विकलः काणो द्वाभ्याम् अन्धः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ इति अज्ञात्वापीत्य् अर्थः । यथा पद-न्यास-स्थानम् अतिक्रम्य शीघ्रं परतः पद-न्यासेन गतिर् धावनं, तद्वद् अत्रापि किञ्चित् किञ्चिद् अतिक्रम्यातिशीघ्रानुष्ठानं धावनम् । तथानुतिष्ठन्न् अपि न स्खलेत्, न प्रत्यवायी स्यात् । तथा न पतेत्, फलान् न भ्रश्येत् । [ब्राह्मणादीनाम् उक्तान् अपि धर्मान् कांश्चिद् अकुर्वाणो भागवतान् धर्मान् श्रवण-कीर्तनादीन् कुर्वाणस् तत्-फलं प्राप्नुयाद् इत्य् अर्थः ।] ॥३५॥
word_for_word: the ease expressed by the word 'easily'
as in yoga and the like
one would not be obstructed by obstacles
Śruti and Smṛti are both eyes
passing beyond the place where the foot is set
one would not incur an adverse result
one would not miss the result
the duties of Brahmins and others
performing bhāgavata duties such as hearing and chanting
entries.literal_english: He explains the ease expressed by the word 'easily': relying on these duties, one is not obstructed by difficulties as in yoga and similar disciplines. Even running with one's eyes closed, one does not stumble in these bhāgavata duties. Closing the eyes means ignorance; the cited verse calls Śruti and Smṛti the two eyes, and one who lacks one is one-eyed while one who lacks both is blind. As a runner may pass beyond the exact place for a foot and still not stumble, so one who performs these practices quickly, even overlooking some steps, does not incur an adverse result or lose the fruit. Even one who omits some duties of Brahmins and others but performs bhāgavata practices such as hearing and chanting obtains their fruit.
entries.note: The quoted Śruti–Smṛti verse and the source's bracketed qualification are retained in the Sanskrit field; the source groups no additional verse with 11.2.35.

entries.sanskrit: ननु के ते भागवता धर्माः ? ईश्वरार्पितानि सर्व-कर्माण्य् अपीत्य् आह---कायेन इति। आत्मना चित्तेनाहङ्कारेण वा । अनुसृतो यः स्वभावस् तस्मात् । अयम् अर्थः---न केवलं विधितः कृतम् एवेति नियमः । स्वभावानुसारि लौकिकम् अपीति । तथा च श्री-गीतासु--- यत् करोषि यद् अश्नासि यज् जुहोषि ददासि यत् । यत् तपस्यसि कौन्तेय तत् कुरुष्व मद्-अर्पणम् ॥ [गीता ९.२७] इति । यद् वा, ननु कायादीनाम् एव कर्म नात्मन इत्य् आशङ्क्याह---अध्यासेनानुसृताद् ब्राह्मणत्वादि-स्वभावाद् यद् यत् करोति इत्य् अर्थः । तत् सकलं परस्मै परमेश्वराय नारायणाय इति समर्पयेत् । तथा सति सकलम् अपि कर्म भागवतो धर्मो भवतीति भावः ॥३६॥
word_for_word: but what are those bhāgavata duties?
even all actions offered to the Lord
not only what is done by injunction
even worldly conduct according to one's nature
सकलम् अपि कर्म भागवतो धर्मः भवति
entries.literal_english: One may ask what the bhāgavata duties are. The instruction is to offer every action performed by body, mind or ego, and every action that follows one's assumed nature. This rule is not limited to acts prescribed by injunction; ordinary worldly conduct in accordance with that nature is included. Whatever one does should be offered to the Supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa, and then all action becomes bhāgavata dharma.
entries.note: The source quotes Bhagavad-gītā 9.27 as its supporting example; that citation remains in the Sanskrit source field.

entries.sanskrit: ननु किम् एवं परमेश्वर-भजनेन ? अज्ञान-कल्पित-भयस्य ज्ञानैक-निवर्तकत्वात्, इत्य् आशङ्क्याह---भयम् इति । यतो भयं तन्-मायया भवेत्, ततो बुद्धिमान् तम् एव आभजेद् उपासीत । ननु भयं द्वितीयाभिनिवेशतः स्यात् । स च देहाद्य्-अहङ्कारतः । स च स्वरूपास्फुरणात्। किम् अत्र तस्य माया करोति ? अत आह---ईशाद् अपेतस्येति । ईश-विमुखस्य तन्-मायया अस्मृतिः स्वरूपास्फूर्तिर् भवति । ततो विपर्ययो देहोऽस्मीति । ततो द्वितीयाभिनिवेशाद् भयं भवति । एवं हि प्रसिद्धं लौकिकीष्व् अपि मायासु । उक्तं च भगवता--- दैवी ह्य् एषा गुण-मयी मम माया दुरत्यया । माम् एव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायाम् एतां तरन्ति ते ॥ [गीता ७.१४] इति । एकया अव्यभिचारिण्या भजेत् । किं च, गुरु-देवतात्मा गुरुर् एव देवता ईश्वर आत्मा प्रेष्ठश् च यस्य, तथा-दृष्टिः सन्न् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३७॥
word_for_word: from ego concerning the body and the rest
from the failure of one's true nature to shine
of one turned away from the Lord
from fixation on a second, fear
the guru is deity and self
entries.literal_english: Fear arises through the Lord's māyā; therefore the intelligent person should worship Him alone. Fear comes from fixation on a second thing, which arises from ego centered on the body and from failure to experience one's true nature. For one who has turned away from the Lord, His māyā produces forgetfulness, then the error 'I am the body,' and then fear born of duality. One should worship with undeviating devotion, seeing the guru as deity and as one's most beloved self.
entries.note: The source includes a citation of Bhagavad-gītā 7.14 after explaining the sequence from forgetfulness to fear.

entries.sanskrit: ननु विषय-विक्षिप्त-चित्तस्य कुतोऽव्यभिचारिणी भक्तिः संभवति ? कुतस्तराम् अभयं ? तत्र न तावद् विषयो नाम वास्तवोऽस्ति, किन्तु मनो-विलास-मात्रम् । अतो मनो-नियमनेन भजनाद् अभयं स्याद्, इत्य् आह---अविद्यमानोऽपीति । द्वयः द्वैत-प्रपञ्चः । ध्यातुः पुंसो धिया मनसा स्वप्नश् च मनो-रथश् च यथेत्य् अर्थः । तत् तस्मात् कर्माणि सङ्कल्पयति विकल्पयति च यन् मनस् तन् निरुन्ध्यान् नियच्छेत् । ततश् चैकया भक्त्या भजनाद् अभयं स्याद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३८॥
word_for_word: of one whose mind is scattered among objects
merely a play of the mind
through worship by restraining the mind
of the meditator, through the mind
a dream and a mental fancy
entries.literal_english: How can unwavering devotion and fearlessness arise for a mind scattered among sense objects? The objects are not ultimately real; they are only a play of the mind. By worshipping while restraining the mind, one becomes fearless. The field of duality is like a dream or mental fancy for the meditator, and the mind is what projects and differentiates its actions and possibilities. That mind should be restrained; then single-minded devotion yields fearlessness.

entries.sanskrit: एतद् अत्यत्नाशक्यम् इत्य् आशङ्क्य सुगमं मार्गम् आह---शृण्वन्न् इति । तद्-अर्थकानि तान्य् एव जन्मानि कर्माणिचार्थो येषां, तानि । एतान्य् अपि साकल्येन ज्ञातुम् अशक्यानीत्य् आशङ्क्याह---यानि लोकेगीतानि प्रसिद्धानि, तानि शृण्वन् गायंश् च विचरेत् । असङ्गो निःस्पृहः ॥३९॥
word_for_word: births and deeds whose purpose is that
which are celebrated in the world
entries.literal_english: If this seems exceedingly difficult, he gives an easy path. One should hear and sing the births and deeds of the Lord whose purpose is that [divine teaching], insofar as they are celebrated in the world, and move through life without attachment or longing.

entries.sanskrit: एवं च भजतः सम्प्राप्त-प्रेम-लक्षण-भक्ति-योगस्य संसार-धर्मातीतां गतिम् आह---एवम् इति । एवं-व्रतं वृत्तं यस्य सः । स्व-प्रियस्य हरेर् नाम-कीर्त्या जातोऽनुरागः प्रेम यस्य सः । अत एव द्रुत-चित्तः श्लथद्-धृदयः । कदाचिद् भक्त-पराजितं भगवन्तम् आकलय्य उच्चैर्हसति । एतावन्तं कालम् उपेक्षितोऽस्मीति रोदिति । अत्यौत्सुक्याद् रौति क्रोशति । हे हरे ! माम् अनुगृहाणेति अतिहर्षेण गायति । जितं जितम् इति नृत्यति । किं दाम्भिकवत् परान् प्रति प्रकाशयितुम् ? न, उन्मादवद् ग्रह-गृहीतवत् । लोक-बाह्यो विवशः ॥४०॥
word_for_word: whose vow or practice is thus
by chanting the name of one's beloved Hari
the Lord conquered by His devotee
entries.literal_english: A person who adopts this practice and develops love by chanting the name of his beloved Hari has a heart melted by devotion. Thinking of the Lord as conquered by His devotee, he sometimes laughs loudly; feeling long neglected, he cries; from intense eagerness he wails; in great joy he sings and dances, exclaiming that Hari has won. He does not display these acts to impress others; like one possessed by madness, he becomes helpless and goes beyond worldly convention.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, खम् इति । सत्त्वानि भूतानि । आकाशादि यत् किञ्चिद् भूत-मात्रं हरेः शरीरम् इति मत्वा प्रणमेत् । सम्भावनायां लिङ् ॥४१॥
word_for_word: whatever consists of the elements beginning with ether
the optative is used for an intended or contemplated act
entries.literal_english: He should regard every being and everything made of the elements beginning with ether as Hari's body and bow to it. The optative form indicates the contemplated or appropriate act of bowing.

entries.sanskrit: नन्व् इयम् आरूढ-योगानाम् अपि बहुभिर् जन्मभिर् दुर्लभा गतिः कथं नाम कीर्तन-मात्रेणैकस्मिन्न् एव जन्मनि भवेत् ? इत्य् आशङ्क्य स-दृष्टान्तम् आह---भक्तिर् इति प्रपद्यमानस्य हरिं भजतः पुंसो भक्तिः प्रेम-लक्षणा । परेशानुभवः प्रेमास्पद-भगवद्-रूप-स्फूर्तिः । तया निवृत्तस्य ततोऽन्यत्र गृहादिषु विरक्तिर् इत्य् एष त्रिक एक-कालो भजन-सम-काल एव स्यात् । यथाश्नतो भुञ्जानस्य तुष्टिः सुखं पुष्टिर् उदर-भरणं क्षुण्-निवृत्तिश् च प्रतिघासं स्युः । उपलक्षणम् एतत् । प्रतिसिक्थम् अपि यथा स्युस् तद्वत् । एवम् एकैकस्मिन् भजने किंचित् प्रेमादि-त्रिके जायमानेऽनुवृत्त्या भजतः परम-प्रेमादि जायते । बहु-ग्रास-भोजिन इव परम-तुष्ट्य्-आदि ॥४२॥
word_for_word: the goal is difficult to attain over many births
for a person taking refuge in and worshipping Hari
as satisfaction, nourishment and removal of hunger for one who eats
entries.literal_english: How can a goal difficult even for accomplished yogīs across many births arise in one life from mere chanting? For a person who takes refuge in Hari and worships Him, three things arise together: devotion marked by love, direct experience of the Supreme Lord, and dispassion from everything else. As satisfaction, nourishment and the ending of hunger arise together with each mouthful of food, so the triad appears with each act of worship; through continued practice it develops into supreme love and the corresponding fullness.

entries.sanskrit: ततश् च भगवत्-प्रसादेन कृतार्थो भवतीत्य् आह---इत्य् अच्युताङ्घ्रिम् इति ॥४३॥
word_for_word: with the words 'the feet of Acyuta'
entries.literal_english: Then, through the Lord's grace, he becomes fulfilled; this is stated in the verse beginning 'the feet of Acyuta.'

entries.sanskrit: भागवतस्य भवन्तीत्य् उक्ते तस्य लक्षणं पृच्छति---अथेति । यद्-धर्मो यस्मिन् धर्मे परिनिष्ठितः । यादृशो यत्-स्वभावः । यथा चरति वर्तते ब्रूते वा । यैश् च लिङ्गैर् भगवतः प्रियो भवति ॥४४॥
word_for_word: he asks for that person's characteristics
of what kind, of what nature
he becomes dear to the Lord
entries.literal_english: Having been told that such qualities belong to the bhāgavata devotee, the king asks for the devotee's characteristics: in what dharma he is established, what his nature is, how he acts or speaks, and by which signs he is recognized as dear to the Lord.

entries.sanskrit: यद् धर्म इत्य् अस्योत्तरम् आह त्रयेण---सर्व-भूतेष्व् इति । आत्मनः स्वस्य सर्व-भूतेषु ब्रह्म-भावेन समन्वयं पश्येत् । तथा ब्रह्म-रूपे आत्मन्य् अधिष्ठाने भूतानि च यः पश्येत् । यद् वा---आततत्वात् प्रमातृत्वाद् आत्मा हि परमो हरिः इति तन्त्रोक्तेर् आत्मनो हरेः सर्व-भूतेषु मशकादिष्व् अपि नियन्तृत्वेन वर्तमानस्य भगवद्-भावं निरतिशयैश्वर्यम् एव यः पश्येत्, न तु तस्य तारतम्यम् । तथात्मनि हराव् एव भूतानि च यः पश्येत् । कथम्भूते ? भगवति अप्रच्युतैश्वर्यादि-रूपे । न पुनर् जड-मलिन-भूताश्रयत्वेन जाड्यादि-प्रसक्त्या ऐश्वर्यादि-च्युतिं पश्येत् । स सर्वत्र परिपूर्णं भगवत्-तत्त्वं पश्यन् भागवतोत्तम इत्य् अर्थः ॥४५॥
word_for_word: in the self, the Brahman-form substratum
the divine status of Hari, the Self
present in all beings as their controller
in Bhagavān whose sovereignty and other qualities do not decline
the complete reality of Bhagavān everywhere
entries.literal_english: He answers the question about the devotee's dharma with three verses, beginning here. One should see one's own self in all beings as Brahman, and beings in the self as the Brahman-form foundation. Alternatively, one should see Hari's divine presence in every being, even the smallest, as the unsurpassed controller, without imposing gradations on that sovereignty; likewise one sees all beings in Hari, the Self. Bhagavān's sovereignty does not diminish because He is present in bodies that are inert or impure. Seeing the complete reality of Bhagavān everywhere is the mark of the foremost devotee.
entries.note: Śrīdhara says the answer to the question in 11.2.44 is given in three verses; the source then supplies separate Śrīdhara blocks for 11.2.45, 11.2.46 and 11.2.47.

entries.sanskrit: प्रेम च मैत्री च कृपा च उपेक्षा च, ता ईश्वरादिषु चतुर्षु यः करोति स मध्यमो भागवतः । एवम्-भूतस्य भेदस्य दर्शनात् ॥४६॥
word_for_word: these toward the four categories beginning with the Lord
that person is a middle-level bhāgavata
entries.literal_english: He who shows love, friendship, compassion and indifference toward the four categories beginning with the Lord is a middle-level devotee. His middle status is due to his perception of distinctions among those four kinds of persons.

entries.sanskrit: अर्चायां प्रतिमायां पूजामीहते करोति, न तद्-भक्तेष्व् अन्येषु च सुतरां न करोति । प्राकृतः प्रकृत-प्रारम्भः । अधुनैव प्रारब्ध-भक्तिः शनैर् उत्तमो भविष्यतीत्य् अर्थः ॥४७॥
word_for_word: in the image used for worship
especially he does not perform it
one at the beginning of material nature
entries.literal_english: The person who performs worship of Hari in the image but does not worship His devotees, or others, is called a prākṛta, one still at the beginning of material conditioning. His devotion has only recently begun, and in time he will become advanced.

entries.sanskrit: पुनर् अष्टभिः श्लोकैर् अभ्यर्हित-त्वद्-उत्तम-भागवतस्यैव लक्षणान्य् आह---गृहीत्वापीति । श्री-वासुदेव-विष्ट-चेता न गृह्णाति तावद् इन्द्रियैर् अर्थान्गृहीत्वापीत्य् अपि-शब्दार्थः । इदं विश्वम् ॥४८॥
word_for_word: of the most highly esteemed foremost devotee just described
one whose mind is pervaded by Śrī Vāsudeva
does not take up / become caught by
even after the senses take their objects
entries.literal_english: In eight further verses he gives the characteristics of the highly esteemed foremost devotee. Even while the senses take in their objects, one whose mind is filled with Śrī Vāsudeva does not become caught by them; this whole universe is [seen as His māyā].

entries.sanskrit: किं च देहादीनां संसार-धर्मैर् जन्माप्य् अयादिभिर् यो हरेः स्मृत्याऽविमुह्यमानः स भागवत-प्रधानः । तत्र देहस्य जन्माप्ययौ । प्राणस्य क्षुत्-पिपासे । मनसो भयम् । बुद्धेस् तर्पस् तृष्णा । इन्द्रियाणां कृच्छ्रं श्रमस् तैः ॥४९॥
word_for_word: by the worldly conditions of the body and the rest
birth and decay of the body
hunger and thirst of the vital force
satiety and craving of the intellect
hardship and fatigue of the senses
entries.literal_english: He is a foremost devotee who, by remembering Hari, is not bewildered by the worldly conditions of body and the other faculties: birth and decay belong to the body, hunger and thirst to the vital force, fear to the mind, satiety and craving to the intellect, and hardship and fatigue to the senses.

entries.sanskrit: कामश् च कर्माणि च वीजानि च वसनास् तेषाम् । वसुदेव एवैक-निलय आश्रयो यस्य सः । एतेन गृहीत्वापि [भा।पु। ११.२.४८] इत्य्-आदि-श्लोक-त्रयेण द्वेष-हर्ष-मोह-कामादि-रहितश् चरतीति यथा चरतीत्य् एतस्योत्तरम् उक्तम् ॥५०॥
word_for_word: the seeds and latent impressions of these
Vāsudeva alone is the sole abode
by the three verses beginning 'even after taking'
free from hatred, elation, delusion, desire and the rest
this is the answer to 'how he behaves'
entries.literal_english: Desire, action, their seeds and their latent impressions have Vāsudeva alone as the refuge of the person described. Through the three verses beginning 'even after taking,' Śrīdhara answers the question of how such a devotee behaves: he lives free from hatred, elation, delusion, desire and similar disturbances.

entries.sanskrit: यैर् लिङ्गैर् भगवत्-प्रिय इत्य् अस्योत्तरम् आह---न यस्येति । जन्म सत्-कुलम् । कर्म तप-आदि । जातयोऽनुलोम-प्रतिलोम-ज मूर्धाव् असिक्तादयः । अस्मिन् देहे । अहङ्कार-रहितैः सत्-कुल-कर्मादि-लिङ्गैर् हरेः प्रियो भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥५१॥
word_for_word: the signs by which he is dear to Bhagavān
he gives the answer to this question
castes born through anuloma and pratiloma unions
through signs such as noble family and conduct
entries.literal_english: He now answers the question about the signs by which a devotee is dear to Bhagavān. Birth in a noble family, conduct such as austerity, and caste designations—including those arising from anuloma or pratiloma unions and the mūrdhāvasikta class—are related to the body. When these signs are free from ego, a person is dear to Hari.

entries.sanskrit: वित्तेषु स्वीयं परकीयम् इति आत्मनि स्वः पर इति ॥५२॥
entries.literal_english: With respect to possessions, the notions are 'mine' and 'another's'; with respect to the self or body, they are 'one's own' and 'another.'

entries.sanskrit: किं च, त्रि-भुवन-विभव-हेतवेऽपि त्रैलोक्य-राज्यार्थम् अपि लवार्धम् अपि निमिषार्धम् अपि भगवत्-पदारविन्द-भजनाद् यो न चलति स वैष्णवाग्र्यः । ननु लवार्ध-मात्र-भजनोपरमे चैतावान् लाभो भवेत् । तत् कुतो न चलेत् ? तत्राह---अकुण्ठ-स्मृतिः भगवत्-पदतोऽन्यत् सारं नास्तीत्य् एवं-रूपाकुण्ठानपगता स्मृतिर् यस्य सः। भगवत्-पदारविन्दाद् अन्यत् सारं नास्तीति कुतः ? अत आह---अजिते हराव् एवात्मा येषां तथाभूतैः सुरादिभिर् अपि दुर्लभात्, किन्तु केवलं विमृग्यात् । तद्-अपेक्षया सर्वस्य तुच्छत्वं स्मरन् यो न चलतीत्य् अर्थः ॥५३॥
word_for_word: even for the sovereignty of the three worlds
from worship of the Lord's lotus feet
that person is the foremost Vaiṣṇava
there is no essence apart from the Lord's feet
those whose self is in unconquered Hari
difficult even for the gods and others
compared with that, everything else is insignificant
entries.literal_english: Even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, not even for half a lava or half a blink does the foremost Vaiṣṇava deviate from worship of the Lord's lotus feet. His remembrance is unbroken because he knows that nothing else has value. The state of having one's self in unconquered Hari is difficult even for the gods, who seek it; remembering the insignificance of everything else by comparison, he does not turn away.

entries.sanskrit: अपि च विषयाभिसन्धिना चलनं कामेनातिसन्तापे सति भवेत्, स तु भगवत्-सेवा-निर्वृतौ न संभवतीत्य् आह---भगवत इति । उरु-विक्रमौ च ताव् अङ्घ्री च तयोः शाखा अङ्गुलयस् तासु नखानि च तानि मणयश् च तेषां चन्द्रिका शीतला दीप्तिस् तया निरस्तः कामादि-तापो यस्मिंस् तस्मिन्न् उपसीदतां भजतां हृदि कथं पुनः सन्तापः प्रभवति ? चन्द्रे उदिते सत्य् अर्कस्य ताप इव । न यस्य स्वः पर इत्य्-आदिना श्लोक-त्रयेण यादृश इत्य् अस्योत्तरम् उक्तं वेदितव्यम् । यद् ब्रूते [११.२.४४] इत्य् अस्य च हरि-नामानीति ज्ञातव्यम् ॥५४॥
word_for_word: deviation through fixation on sense objects
when there is intense distress from desire
in the joy of serving the Lord
those two feet of the mighty-striding Lord
their moonlike radiance is cool light
the heat of desire and the like is dispelled
in the hearts of those who draw near and worship
as the sun's heat when the moon has risen
entries.literal_english: Deviation caused by fixation on sense objects occurs when desire burns intensely, but it cannot arise in the joy of serving the Lord. The two feet of the mighty-striding Lord are imagined as a wish-tree: the toes are its branches, the nails are jewels, and their cool moonlike radiance dispels the heat of desire and the rest in the hearts of worshippers. How could that heat return, just as the sun's heat cannot prevail when the moon has risen?

entries.sanskrit: उक्त-समस्त-लक्षण-सारम् आह---विसृजतीति । हरिर् एव स्वयं साक्षाद् यस्य हृदयं न विसृजति न मुञ्चति । कथं-भूतः ? अवशेनाप्य् अभिहित-मात्रोऽप्य् अघौघं नाशयति यः, सः । तत् किं न विसृजति ? यतः प्रणय-रशनया धृतं हृदये निबद्धम् अङ्घ्रि-पद्मं यस्य स भागवत-प्रधान उक्तो भवति ॥५५॥
word_for_word: the essence of all the stated characteristics
whose lotus feet are held fast
he is called the foremost devotee
entries.literal_english: He now states the essence of all the characteristics: Hari Himself does not leave the heart of the person whose lotus feet are held there by the cord of love. Hari destroys the mass of sins even when His name is uttered involuntarily or only once; such a person is called the foremost devotee.
